body: Lopez-Lira & Tang: weak headline-sentiment signal (~51%); look-ahead/memorisation bias inflates LLM backtests. Alpha Arena S1 crypto: Qwen +22%, GPT-5 −62%; S1.5 stocks: 6/32 positive. AIEQ ETF ~9.7%/yr vs S&P ~14.2% over ~9 yrs. FinanceBench: retrieval-based answers often wrong. Use AI for reading, forensics, red-teaming.
title: AI doesn't pick winners by itself

body: Nifty trailing P/E: a Stable Investor study (data to 2015) found that from P/E above 24, average subsequent 3/5/7-year returns were -5.1%/2.7%/9.9% a year, while from P/E below 12 the 5-year return averaged ~29% a year. Freefincal found every instance of a negative 5-year Nifty return started from P/E >=24.5, though over 3 years P/E was a weak predictor (negative 3-year returns from P/E >=22 only ~43% of the time). MoneyWorks4Me: entry above 22-25x led to poor 3-5 year returns, with the effect fading over 10-15 years. Sensex peaks: ~28x (2000) and ~27-28x (Jan 2008) both preceded ~60% crashes; troughs at ~12x (2008-09) preceded strong multi-year gains. Market cap/GDP: near 150% (2007) preceded roughly zero Sensex returns from Jan 2008 to late 2013; ~56% (Mar 2020) preceded a doubling within a year; 115-122% (2021) preceded a flat 2022; ~140% (mid-2024, a 15-year high) preceded the 2024-25 correction. Long-run average Sensex P/E ~18.5-19x; long-run mcap/GDP average ~76-81% (figures vary by GDP base). Caveats: index composition (more financials, fewer commodities) and lower rates may lift 'normal' P/Es; earnings-cycle troughs inflate P/E (Mar 2020). Rule: above ~24x trailing Nifty P/E or >~120% mcap/GDP, expect low single-digit 5-year returns; below ~14-15x or <~70%, expect high returns.
title: Valuation levels that preceded bad (and great) 5-year Indian returns
